name: Beyond Energy: When Sustainability Dimensions Reshape LLM Serving Decisions (PRISM)
problem: LLM serving has energy, carbon, water and biodiversity impacts, but these are evaluated in isolation, so it is unclear when they point at DIFFERENT serving decisions and silently conflict.
mechanism: Unified framework that separates WHICH LEVER controls WHICH DIMENSION: computing configuration determines energy consumption, whereas WHERE and WHEN serving is deployed determines its carbon, water and biodiversity impacts. Identifies the conditions under which dimensions diverge, quantifies cross-dimensional regret, and balances the four jointly — including that embodied impacts can break configuration invariance once they exceed a lifecycle crossover boundary.
speedup_reported: Per the arXiv abstract, in REGIONAL-ROUTING experiments PRISM reduces median worst-case regret by 50.2% relative to the strongest baseline. This is a REGRET metric across sustainability dimensions, not a throughput or cost-speedup — do not compare it to a serving engine's efficiency number. The 50.2% is specific to the paper's regional-routing experimental setup.
notes: Venue arxiv-preprint (41-page preprint, no venue claim). The green-inference slice is overwhelmingly energy-per-query work that silently treats carbon as a multiple of joules; this paper's claim is precisely that the equivalence BREAKS once you count water and embodied impacts — deployment region and time can overturn the ranking that an energy-only optimisation would give you. That is the argument worth remembering even if you never read the paper.
